newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific labor talks underway.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific labor talks underway.

text.p: Union Pacific Corp. said Tuesday negotiations with union leadership representing Southern Pacific Rail Corp. are underway with ratification expected in 1997 and 1998.

Under conditions imposed by the U.S. Surface Transporation Board of the Department of Transportation, labour agreements between Union Pacific and the unions must be negotiated before the two rail systems can be fully integrated.
The merger between the two rail systems was compeleted last September with total implementation, including merger of operations, expected to take at least two years.

In a quarterly filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Union Pacific said terms of ratified and pending labour agreements are not expected to have a material adverse effect on the corporation's operating results.

Labour leaders of some regional operating, shopcraft, carmen and clerical unions have negotiated agreements relating to the consolidation and coordination of Union Pacific and Southern Pacific operations, Union Pacfic said in the filing.
The four regional unions collectively represent about 45 percent of Southern Pacific's unionized workforce.
